key_insight: GameHorizon introduces a unified way to evaluate gameplay AI across multiple temporal horizons, capturing not just reflexive actions but also instruction following, planning, and long-horizon control. It aims to make game-based evaluation more realistic, consistent, and broadly comparable.
problem_solved: Current game AI datasets and benchmarks are fragmented: many cover only a limited set of games, omit language-based instructions, or depend on noisy online rollouts that make evaluation unstable. This paper addresses the need for a single suite that can assess gameplay abilities at different time scales in a more reliable way.
method: Builds a unified data and evaluation suite for gameplay tasks spanning multiple horizons of decision-making.
Measures capabilities from short-term action control to longer-term planning and instruction decomposition.
Reduces evaluation variance by moving away from purely high-variance online rollouts toward more controlled benchmarking.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, GameHorizon offers a more comprehensive benchmark for comparing models on real gameplay competence, not just narrow skill slices. It can help researchers diagnose where models fail across visual perception, reasoning, and control.
visual_elements: A horizon timeline showing short-, mid-, and long-term gameplay decisions
A pipeline diagram linking visual input, language instructions, planning, and action execution
A comparison chart of existing benchmarks vs. GameHorizon across game coverage, language support, and evaluation stability
Icons representing perception, language, planning, and control
paper_title: GameHorizon Suite: Multi-Horizon Data and Evaluation in Gameplay
paper_authors: Yiran Wang, Xingyilang Yin, Junfu Pu, Guangzhi Wang, Kaifeng Li
